h1: The 6 Best Privacy Screens for 21:9 Ultrawide Monitors, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 privacy screens for 30 and 34 inch 21:9 ultrawide and curved monitors, compared on fit, coatings and pack size.
summary: The 2-pack 34 inch curved-compatible privacy screen is our top choice, because it lists 21:9 support for curved panels and gives you a spare sheet. The Mamol 34 inch filter is the best all-rounder with anti-glare, blue-light and anti-scratch coatings, and the ACONETMAX 30 inch is the pick for smaller ultrawides. Shoppers on a tight budget should consider the 34 inch removable filter, while the ZYY lists a precise active area for careful sizing.
intro: Ultrawide monitors punish sloppy sizing. A 16:9 filter simply will not cover a 21:9 panel, and even within the 21:9 family a 30 inch screen and a 34 inch screen need different sheets. Pick the wrong size and you are left with a dark band on one side and a bright strip on the other.

Our ranking therefore starts with fit, then moves to curvature, coatings and pack size. We reviewed six ultrawide privacy screens from their listings, covering 30 and 34 inch sizes, flat and curved compatibility and the finish claims each seller makes. Nothing here relies on a lab result, and where a listing is thin we treat the missing detail as a reason to be careful.

products.name: 2-Pack 34 Inch Privacy Screen for Curved Monitors, 21:9
products.verdict: A removable pair of 34 inch sheets built for curved 21:9 monitors.
products.description:
This listing is a pair of removable privacy sheets for 34 inch curved monitors with a 21:9 aspect ratio. It sits in the $100 to $200 bracket, which is the highest price tier here and reflects that two large sheets come in the box.

It ranks first because it addresses the main challenge of the ultrawide category head on: a 34 inch curved panel is wide and bowed, and a filter that ignores the curve can lift away from the glass. The listing states curved compatibility, and a second sheet covers a spare or a twin-monitor desk. Where it loses ground is cost, since the pair lands well above the single-sheet options below.

Buy it if you run a 34 inch curved ultrawide and want a ready spare, or two screens. Skip it if you only need one sheet and want to save money.
cons: A single sheet is enough for many
products.idealFor: Owners of 34 inch curved ultrawides, or two screens.
products.skipIf: You need only one sheet and a low price.

products.name: Mamol 34 Inch Curved Computer Privacy Screen Filter
products.verdict: A curved 34 inch filter with anti-glare, blue-light and anti-scratch coatings.
products.description:
The Mamol is a single filter for 34 inch, 21:9 curved monitors, with anti-glare, blue-light filtering and anti-scratch surface features listed. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Second place is earned because it packs the most surface features of the single-sheet options. Anti-glare helps in rooms with windows, since a filter can otherwise add reflections to an already glossy panel. An anti-scratch layer matters on a sheet you remove and replace often. It trails the top pick only because it comes as one sheet, and blue-light filtering claims are the sort of thing worth treating as a bonus, not a reason to buy.

Choose it for a single 34 inch curved monitor in a bright room. Skip it if you need a spare sheet or the cheapest possible filter.
cons: Blue-light claim is a minor perk
products.idealFor: A bright office with one curved 34 inch screen.
products.skipIf: You want a spare or a rock-bottom price.

products.name: ACONETMAX 30 Inch Privacy Screen Filter for Curved 21:9 Ultrawide
products.verdict: A 30 inch curved 21:9 filter with anti-glare, blue-light, UV and anti-scratch layers.
products.description:
The ACONETMAX is sized for 30 inch, 21:9 curved ultrawide monitors and lists anti-glare, blue-light, UV protection and anti-scratch features. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It takes third place because it is the only listing in this group for the smaller 30 inch class that carries the full set of surface features. Size is the real selling point: 30 inch ultrawides are far less common than 34 inch ones, and their owners have fewer filter options. UV protection is a minor extra for a monitor that never sees sun, but it does no harm. It ranks below the 34 inch picks since those fit the more popular panel size.

Buy it if you own a 30 inch curved ultrawide and want a coated sheet. Skip it if your monitor is a 34 inch, since this sheet will be too short.
cons: UV claim has little real use
products.idealFor: Owners of 30 inch curved ultrawide monitors.

products.name: APeiSi 30 Inch Privacy Screen Filter for 21:9 Curved Ultrawide Gaming Monitor
products.verdict: A 30 inch filter marketed at gamers, with anti-glare and anti-blue-light coatings.
products.description:
The APeiSi is another 30 inch, 21:9 curved filter, positioned for gaming monitors and listing anti-glare and anti-blue-light features. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Fourth place fits, as it matches the ACONETMAX on size and curve, but its coating list is shorter and it makes no UV or anti-scratch claim. A gaming focus is mostly marketing here, since a privacy filter always dims and narrows the image to some degree, which is a real concern for fast games where you want the widest viewing angle and brightest panel. If you game seriously, plan to remove the filter when you play.

Pick it if you want a 30 inch curved sheet and like to switch it off for games. Skip it if your priority is the best surface protection.
cons: No scratch or UV claim listed
products.idealFor: 30 inch ultrawide users who also game.
products.skipIf: You want the toughest surface layer.

products.name: 34 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter for 21:9 Widescreen Monitors
products.verdict: A low-cost removable 34 inch sheet with anti-glare and blue-light filtering.
products.description:
This single 34 inch sheet is sized for 21:9 widescreen monitors and lists anti-glare, blue-light filtering and removable use. It falls in the $25 to $50 bracket, the lowest tier in the ranking.

It ranks fifth because the price is the main reason to choose it. The listing mentions a 21:9 shape but does not say curved, so owners of bowed panels should confirm fit before buying, since a flat sheet on a curved screen may sit loosely at the edges. Removable use is helpful, as you can lift it off for work that needs full brightness.

Buy it for a flat 34 inch ultrawide on a limited budget. Skip it if your panel is curved and you want a listed curved match.
products.idealFor: Flat 34 inch ultrawides on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: Your monitor has a pronounced curve.

products.name: ZYY 34 Inch Diagonal Curved Computer Privacy Screen
products.verdict: A curved-compatible sheet that publishes an exact 31 1/4 by 13 3/8 inch active area.
products.description:
The ZYY is a 34 inch diagonal curved-compatible privacy screen, and its listing gives an active area of 31 1/4 by 13 3/8 inches. It sits in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Last place suits it, since the page lists dimensions but little else: no coating details, no pack information and no features to compare against the Mamol. The published measurements are valuable, though, since they let you hold a tape measure to your screen and confirm that the sheet will cover the visible panel without guessing. Many ultrawide buyers skip this check and end up with a sheet that is a few millimeters off.

Get it if you like to verify the size before you buy, and you own a curved 34 inch panel. Skip it if you want a filter with listed anti-glare or anti-scratch layers.
products.idealFor: Careful buyers who measure before ordering.
products.skipIf: You want listed anti-glare or scratch layers.

methodology.description: Anti-glare, anti-scratch, blue-light and UV claims were compared, with more weight on glare and scratch resistance than on tint claims.

whatMatters.detail: Ultrawide sizes differ by inches, and a 21:9 label alone does not tell you the visible area. Measure the active screen width and height with a tape and compare it to the listing, as the ZYY allows. A sheet that is a few millimeters short leaves a bright band.

A curved monitor bows toward you, and a flat sheet can sit away from the glass at the edges. That creates gaps, glare and a loose feel. Look for the word curved in the listing, as on the Mamol and ACONETMAX.

A privacy layer blocks side light, which also makes the image dimmer for you. On a big ultrawide the effect is more noticeable near the screen edges because you view them at an angle. Raise brightness a little, and choose a removable sheet if you switch tasks.

Anti-glare reduces reflections from windows, and anti-scratch protects the sheet when you remove it. Blue-light filtering warms the image and is a small perk. Look for glare and scratch claims first, since they affect daily use.

Most filters are removable and attach with adhesive strips, clips or mounting tabs, which can vary across brands. Check how the sheet fixes in place and whether it leaves residue. A removable design lets you clear the view when you need it.

faq.q: Will a 16:9 privacy screen fit an ultrawide?
faq.a: No. A 16:9 sheet is too narrow and too tall for a 21:9 panel, so you must buy a sheet made for the ultrawide shape. Match both the diagonal size and the aspect ratio.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with ultrawide filters?
faq.a: Buying by diagonal alone. A 34 inch ultrawide and a 34 inch flat 16:9 screen have very different dimensions. Check width and height against the listing.

faq.q: Is the two-pack worth it over a single sheet?
faq.a: If you have two screens or want a spare, yes. For one monitor, the Mamol gives you better surface features at a lower price. The two-pack is mainly about convenience.

faq.q: How do I install a filter on a curved screen?
faq.a: Clean the panel, line the sheet up with the top corners and press it into place gradually from the center outward. Take your time near the edges, where the curve is strongest. Remove any bubbles with a soft cloth.

faq.q: How do I clean the sheet?
faq.a: Use a dry microfiber cloth for dust and a barely damp one for smudges. Avoid sprays and alcohol, which can damage coatings. Store spare sheets flat between uses.

faq.q: Will a privacy filter affect HDR or color work?
faq.a: Yes, it dims the image and can shift colors slightly. For color-critical work or HDR, use a removable sheet and take it off. A filter is better suited to everyday office tasks.

finalTake: For a 34 inch curved ultrawide, the 2-Pack 34 Inch Privacy Screen is the best choice here, with the Mamol filter as the strongest single sheet. Owners of 30 inch panels should look to the ACONETMAX, and budget buyers with flat screens can use the 34 inch widescreen filter. Measure your panel before you order. A privacy screen only works if it covers the whole visible area.
